findings.source_quote: Καθὼς, φημί, κύριε, ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς ἔδειξας, ἐρωτῶ σε, κύριε, ἵνα καθὼς ἄν σε ἐπερωτήσω, οὕτω μοι καὶ δηλώσῃς.
findings.english_quote: “Sir,” I said, “just as you showed me things from the beginning, I ask you to explain them as I ask you about them.”
findings.issue: The second direct address, κύριε, is omitted. The source repeats the respectful address within Hermas’s request; the English retains only its first occurrence.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the second address: “Sir,” I said, “just as you showed me things from the beginning, I ask you, sir, to explain them as I ask you about them.” This proposal requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν, φασί, κοιμηθήσῃ ὡς ἀδελφός, καὶ οὐχ ὡς ἀνήρ.
findings.english_quote: They are retained together with the explicit brother/husband distinction rather than expanded into a different relationship.
findings.issue: The note presents “husband” as the explicit source distinction without disclosing the alternative “man” to readers. The lexical metadata recognizes that alternative, but it is absent from the footnotes. This matters because the choice affects how readers understand the overnight relationship.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected main-text reading, but add a reader-facing note such as: “Or ‘not as a man.’ The Greek word can mean ‘man’ or ‘husband’; this draft chooses ‘husband’ in the context of the contrast with ‘brother.’” Revise note b so that it distinguishes the explicit Greek contrast from the selected interpretation. The proposed note requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Καθὼς, φημί, κύριε, ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς ἔδειξας, ἐρωτῶ σε, κύριε, ἵνα καθὼς ἄν σε ἐπερωτήσω, οὕτω μοι καὶ δηλώσῃς.
findings.english_quote: I said, “Sir, just as you showed me things from the beginning, I ask you to explain them to me as I ask you questions.”
findings.issue: Independent comparison with the Greek shows that the second κύριε is omitted. Shortening the sentence has removed a repeated respectful address within the request.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the second address: “Sir, just as you showed me things from the beginning, I ask you, sir, to explain them to me as I ask you questions.” This proposal requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Νῦν, φησί, τί θέλεις πρῶτον ἀκοῦσαι;
findings.english_quote: He asked, “What do you want to hear first?”
findings.issue: The simplified text omits Νῦν, “now,” which explicitly marks the transition from the account of the overnight stay to the explanation.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the transition: “He asked, ‘Now, what do you want to hear first?’” This proposal requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν, φασί, κοιμηθήσῃ ὡς ἀδελφός, καὶ οὐχ ὡς ἀνήρ.
findings.english_quote: They are retained together with the explicit brother/husband distinction rather than expanded into a different relationship.
findings.issue: The simplified edition independently inherits the same disclosure defect: its reader-facing note treats “husband” as explicit, while the recognized alternative “man” appears only in lexical metadata.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the selected main-text reading and disclose the alternative in a footnote: “Or ‘not as a man.’ The Greek word can mean ‘man’ or ‘husband’; this draft chooses ‘husband’ because it is contrasted with ‘brother.’” Adjust note b accordingly. The proposed wording requires fresh review.

summary: Both editions substantially preserve all nine paragraphs, including the difficult affectionate scene, restrictions on leaving, continual prayer, supper metaphor, and absolute promise to conceal nothing. Minor revisions are needed for omitted wording and reader-facing disclosure of the man/husband alternative. The bracketed second dance expression is retained and its editorial marking disclosed. The conjecture and restoration notes are attributed reports, not fresh manuscript verification; nothing supplied establishes a contradiction requiring replacement of those working readings. This review does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscripts, certify exhaustive collation, or approve proposed replacements without fresh review.
